title: The Most Profitable Final Fantasy Is an MMO From 2002
hook:
In 2012 Square Enix's president said Final Fantasy XI, the 2002 online game, had made more profit than any other Final Fantasy. It is still running in 2026. Have you ever set foot in Vana'diel?
Gameplay is from Shards of Irsa, a game I'm making.
script: Did you know the most profitable Final Fantasy ever made was not a single player game at all? It was Final Fantasy Eleven, an online world called Vana'diel. Square launched it in Japan on May 16, 2002, on the PlayStation Two, with a PC version following later that year. It was the first MMO where players on different platforms shared the same servers. An Xbox 360 version arrived in 2006, so PlayStation, PC and Xbox players could all adventure together. The community grew past half a million players. In June 2012, Square Enix held a fan event celebrating ten years of the game. There, company president Yoichi Wada told the crowd that Final Fantasy Eleven had become the most profitable title in the whole series. That put it above Seven, Ten and every other mainline game released before it. The console servers finally closed on March 31, 2016, after fourteen years. The PC version never stopped. Square Enix nearly ended updates in 2024, but players rallied and the company kept going. It is still online in 2026, with new content arriving this year and a crossover with Final Fantasy Fourteen pulling veterans back home. Have you ever set foot in Vana'diel? Follow for more gaming history.
